newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents higher Thursday as traders expect the market to follow through on its recent strong showing.
But some traders warned the market could be vunerable to a downward correction and said activity was likely to be subdued today ahead of key U.S. green stock data due after the close.
"I think this market may be a little bit overdone," a trader said. "And people are going to step back ahead of the GCA stocks."

Traders expect Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report to show a stock build of some 100,000 60-kg bags in April, although estimates have ranged widely from a slight decrease to a 250,000 to 300,000-bag increase.

Last month, GCA reported stocks of coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose by 111,000 bags in March, to 1,657,000 bags. In April 1996, however, stocks fell by 76,000 bags, to 2,296,000 bags, the GCA said.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures ended mixed, slipping from new contract highs set earlier in the day. July futures finished down 0.55 cent at 240.60 cents a lb after ranging between a new lifetime high of 248.50 and 236.00. Spot May rose 0.50 cent to 261.50 cents, while the back months closed 0.30 to 6.00 higher.
The July/September switch narrowed to 25.10 cents compared with 25.95 cents at the close on Tuesday.

After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 2,375 bags, to 35,412 bags as of May 11. There were 15,790 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
Fundamentally, German statistician F.O. Licht on Thursday put world 1996/97 coffee production at 97.6 million bags, up from its November forecast of 96.5 million bags and 1995/96's 87.7 million bags.

Licht said the upward revision reflected higher output in the robusta sector, which it revised upward to 32.57 million bags against its November estimate of 31.67 million bags. In 1995/96 the robusta crop totalled 29.71 million bags.

Arabica production is expected to come in at 65.05 million bags, marginally higher than November's forecast of 64.78 million bags, Licht said. In 1995/96, arabica production reached 57.97 million bags.

Licht said Brazil output would total 28.5 million bags in 1996/97 against the weather-hit crop of 15.8 million in 1995/96, while Colombian production is expected to fall to 9.6 million from 12.89 million in 1995/96.
London robusta futures edged higher early Thursday, as the market consolidated recent gains. LIFFE July was up $8 at the midday break, to $1,878, after ranging from $1,887 to $1,860.
LIFFE certified coffee stocks rose to 4,858 five-tonne lots in April from 4,008 in March. London traders said the increase was slightly below their expectations.
